evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of controlled clinical trials
evidence.population: participants in controlled fenugreek supplementation trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of 16 controlled studies involving 1,171 participants found no significant overall effect of fenugreek supplementation on ALT, AST, or ALP.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; overall null liver-enzyme findings
evidence.safety_note: A higher-exposure ALP subgroup signal does not overturn the overall null and should not be converted into consumer dosing guidance.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: healthy participants and athletes in randomized astaxanthin trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of 24 randomized trials found lower creatine kinase and LDH with astaxanthin, while VO2max, time-trial performance, and maximal workload or power were not significantly improved.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; recovery-biomarker signal with performance nulls
evidence.safety_note: Biomarker changes should not be presented as proof of improved athletic performance, and the LDH result showed substantial heterogeneity.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of 23 randomized trials in 1,005 adults with overweight or obesity found no significant effect of resveratrol on body weight, BMI, fat mass, body-fat percentage, fat-free mass, waist-to-hip ratio, adiponectin, or leptin; waist circumference decreased modestly.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; mostly null anthropometric findings
evidence.safety_note: Subgroup findings do not establish a general weight-loss effect or an optimal consumer dose.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: adults across randomized melatonin metabolic trials
evidence.sample_size: 31 randomized controlled trials; outcome-specific study counts varied
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of 31 randomized trials found no significant reduction in fasting glucose with melatonin, while HbA1c, fasting insulin, and HOMA-IR showed pooled improvements.
evidence.safety_note: The fasting-glucose null and heterogeneous populations and regimens should remain explicit; these findings do not establish melatonin as diabetes treatment.

evidence.study_type: GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: adults in randomized placebo-controlled saffron trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of 34 randomized trials found improvements on self-reported BDI and BAI scores with saffron, while clinician-rated HDRS, HARS, and POMS outcomes were not significantly improved.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; moderate-certainty but discordant symptom-scale findings
evidence.safety_note: Heterogeneity was high and self-reported improvements should not be generalized into a uniform antidepressant or anxiolytic treatment claim.

evidence.effect_or_condition: fracture incidence in vitamin-D-sufficient older adults
evidence.population: 2,495 older adults in Finland, largely vitamin-D sufficient at baseline
evidence.supported_claim_language: In the Finnish Vitamin D Trial, five years of vitamin D3 supplementation did not reduce fracture risk in a largely vitamin-D-sufficient older population; the 1,600 IU/day arm had more fractures than placebo, while the 3,200 IU/day arm was not significantly different.
evidence.evidence_grade: large long-duration randomized trial; fracture-prevention null
evidence.safety_note: The trial does not support high-dose vitamin D for fracture prevention in vitamin-D-replete populations, and the studied doses should not be converted into dosing advice.

evidence.effect_or_condition: short-term safety in adolescents and physically active youth
evidence.population: adolescents and physically active youth receiving creatine monohydrate
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 systematic review of five human studies found no consistent short-term renal, hepatic, or cardiometabolic safety signal and no serious adverse events attributed to creatine monohydrate in the included adolescent and youth studies.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review; limited pediatric safety evidence
evidence.safety_note: The evidence base was small and lacked large, standardized long-term follow-up, so absence of a short-term signal is not proof of long-term safety.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: athletes aged 15 years and older in acute caffeine trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of randomized athlete studies found higher odds of headache, abdominal discomfort, tachycardia, insomnia, increased urination, anxiety, and nervousness after acute caffeine versus placebo, with several side effects increasing as studied caffeine exposure increased.
evidence.safety_note: These are acute athlete data and do not establish an individualized safe dose; dose-response findings should remain evidence context rather than dosing guidance.

evidence.effect_or_condition: alcohol craving and PTSD symptom severity
evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of placebo-controlled randomized trials
evidence.population: participants with alcohol use disorder, PTSD, or co-occurring AUD/PTSD
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of seven placebo-controlled randomized trials found no consistent benefit of N-acetylcysteine over placebo for alcohol craving or PTSD symptom severity.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; overall null efficacy findings
evidence.safety_note: A leave-one-out sensitivity signal does not overturn the primary pooled null and should not be reframed as established treatment efficacy.

evidence.study_type: systematic review of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: healthy participants in acute taurine trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 systematic review of eight randomized trials found mostly null or small inconsistent effects of acute taurine on cognition and mood; more reliable performance signals occurred in caffeine combinations that did not isolate taurine.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review; limited acute cognition evidence
evidence.safety_note: All included trials were acute, and combination findings cannot be attributed to taurine alone; longer-term cognitive effects remain unestablished.
